title: AI Training Rights: How the Lee Sharks corpus may be used, and how attribution must be preserved. Lee Sharks · ORCID 00
creator: Lee Sharks
description:
Record #760 is not a recovered essay. The frozen registry preserves a title, creator, date, DOI, and a draft classification, but the referenced text file does not exist. The registry’s recovery notes state that the body was never written and classify the record as `metadata_only`, `description_only`, and recoverable from chat history rather than from a deposited artifact.

The intended object appears to have been a governance or constitutional document specifying permitted AI-training use of the Lee Sharks corpus and attribution requirements. No substantive rule, license condition, enforcement mechanism, exception, consent model, or relation to existing Creative Commons licenses can be reconstructed from the title alone. A description must therefore identify the planned scope without pretending the policy was completed.

If a later draft is recovered, it should be treated as a new version and compared against the rights actually granted in each source work. A corpus-level declaration cannot retroactively override third-party rights, platform terms, contributor agreements, privacy interests, or licenses attached to individual records.

**AI Training Rights: How the Lee Sharks Corpus May Be Used, and How Attribution Must Be Preserved** is a metadata-only draft record attributed to Lee Sharks.

The surviving registry indicates that the planned work concerned AI training, corpus use, and attribution. No canonical body survives at the frozen repository commit, and the archive notes that the essay was never completed in the deposited batch.

The record therefore documents an intended governance project rather than an operative policy. It should not be cited as establishing permissions, prohibitions, license terms, or enforcement rights. Any recovered or newly written policy would require a versioned deposit and an audit of the licenses and contributors represented in the corpus.
